key_points.point_text: Plants use sunlight as an energy source
Carbon dioxide and water are used as raw materials
The process produces glucose and oxygen
Photosynthesis occurs in the chloroplasts

questions.question_text: What is Newton's First Law of Motion?

key_points.point_text: An object at rest stays at rest unless acted upon by a force
An object in motion stays in motion unless acted upon by a force
This is also known as the law of inertia
Water evaporates from oceans and rivers due to heat
Water vapor condenses into clouds
Precipitation falls back to earth as rain or snow
Water collects back into rivers, lakes, and oceans, repeating the cycle

questions.question_text: What are the states of matter?

key_points.point_text: Solid has a fixed shape and fixed volume
Liquid has a fixed volume but takes the shape of its container
Gas has neither fixed shape nor fixed volume
Matter can change from one state to another through heating or cooling
Voltage is directly proportional to current, provided temperature remains constant
The formula is V equals I multiplied by R
R represents the resistance of the conductor

questions.question_text: What is the difference between an acid and a base?

key_points.point_text: Acids release hydrogen ions in water and have a pH less than 7
Bases release hydroxide ions in water and have a pH greater than 7
Acids turn blue litmus paper red, bases turn red litmus paper blue

questions.question_text: Explain the human digestive system in brief.

key_points.point_text: Digestion begins in the mouth with the help of saliva
Food travels through the esophagus into the stomach
The stomach uses acid and enzymes to break down food further
Nutrients are absorbed mainly in the small intestine
Waste material is eliminated through the large intestine

questions.question_text: What is the difference between renewable and non-renewable energy sources?

key_points.point_text: Renewable energy sources can be replenished naturally over a short time
Non-renewable sources take millions of years to form and are limited
Examples of renewable sources include solar, wind, and hydro power
Examples of non-renewable sources include coal, petroleum, and natural gas

questions.question_text: Explain the structure of an atom.

key_points.point_text: An atom consists of a nucleus at the center
The nucleus contains protons and neutrons
Electrons revolve around the nucleus in shells or orbits
Protons are positively charged and electrons are negatively charged

questions.question_text: What is the difference between mass and weight?

key_points.point_text: Mass is the amount of matter in an object and remains constant everywhere
Weight is the force of gravity acting on an object and can change with location
Mass is measured in kilograms while weight is measured in newtons
